parameters.name: table_or_column
parameters.description: The table or column from which filters are removed. If omitted entirely, ALL filters from the entire model are removed.
parameters.examNote: Passing a table removes all column filters on that table. Passing individual columns removes only those column filters. Omitting the argument completely clears every filter in the model — use with care.

returnType: Used as a filter modifier inside CALCULATE — returns a modified filter context, not a standalone scalar
summary: REMOVEFILTERS is used exclusively inside CALCULATE as a filter argument. It removes filters from a specified table, one or more columns, or the entire model. Functionally it is identical to ALL() when used as a CALCULATE modifier, but semantically it communicates intent more clearly — the goal is to remove filters, not to return a full table. Microsoft introduced REMOVEFILTERS to make DAX code more readable and self-documenting.

examples.label: Calculate grand total ignoring all filters
examples.explanation: REMOVEFILTERS(Sales) clears every filter on the Sales table — Region, Product, and any others. CALCULATE then evaluates SUM(Sales[Amount]) across all 900 worth of rows regardless of any slicer.

examples.label: Remove filter from one column only
examples.explanation: Only the Product filter is removed. If a Region slicer is set to East, that filter remains active. This gives the total for all products within the selected region.

steps: CALCULATE receives its filter arguments before evaluating the expression
REMOVEFILTERS(Sales) signals DAX to strip all column filters from the Sales table
The expression is evaluated with no Sales filters but all other model filters remain
REMOVEFILTERS() with no arguments strips filters from every table in the model

commonTraps: REMOVEFILTERS() with NO arguments removes ALL filters from every table in the model — this is an extremely broad operation and rarely the correct choice.
REMOVEFILTERS is identical to ALL() when used inside CALCULATE. The difference is only semantic clarity. On the exam, both are correct for the same use case.
REMOVEFILTERS cannot be used standalone outside of CALCULATE. It has no meaning outside a filter context modification.

sqlEquivalent.note: SQL achieves this by simply not including a WHERE clause. In DAX, filters are always active from slicers and visuals, so REMOVEFILTERS is needed to explicitly override them — there is no passive way to ignore the filter context.
